statement: Implement a queue using two stacks, an in-box and an out-box. push lands on the in-box. For pop and front, serve from the out-box - and only when the out-box is empty, move every element from the in-box onto it, which reverses them into arrival order. The first line holds q; each following line is push x, pop, front or size. Print the results of every pop, front and size, space-separated; the empty sentinel is -1. Each element crosses between stacks at most once, so operations cost amortized constant time.

example.input:
7
push 2
push 5
pop
push 9
pop
pop
pop
example.why: The flip reverses 2 and 5 into arrival order; 9 crosses later in its own flip; the last pop meets emptiness.

hint: Flip only when the out-box is empty; elements already there are in correct order.
mistake: Flipping on every operation - correctness survives, the amortized constant does not.
